claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 begins as a homogeneous high-temperature BCC phase.
Slow cooling from the high-temperature BCC state permits substantial atomic diffusion.
Diffusion during slow cooling produces nanoscale clusters or short-range chemically ordered regions.
The locally ordered regions lower the free-energy barrier for nucleation of secondary ordered phases during subsequent isothermal aging.
Slow cooling followed by aging results in a mixed-phase microstructure containing secondary ordered phases.
Rapid quenching freezes a chemically disordered BCC structure and suppresses local chemical ordering.
Rapidly quenched samples largely preserve a metastable, predominantly single-phase BCC structure rather than forming secondary phases.
Slow-cooled and aged samples will contain more detectable local chemical order than rapidly quenched samples.
Slow-cooled and aged samples will contain more secondary ordered phases than rapidly quenched samples.
The proposed mechanism requires cooling and aging conditions that provide sufficient atomic mobility.
The proposed ordering mechanism should not operate during ultra-rapid quenching or thermal exposure too low to activate diffusion.

contradictions.description: The intended comparison concerns cooling rate followed by standardized aging, but the experimental design explicitly assigns aging only to the slow-cooled set and does not state that the quenched set receives the same aging treatment. This would confound cooling history with subsequent thermal exposure.
